rationale: Both are correct backtracking searches. A is a compact recursive helper with a single base case that covers the empty input and the closed-chain check, so it needs no special cases at the top level. It tries both orientations with one loop over the two possible rotations instead of repeating code. Its use of append(chain, ...) on a slice with spare capacity relies on a subtle sharing property. That is safe here, because each recursion depth only writes its own slot, but it deserves a comment. Copying the rest of the list on every step is a little wasteful. B avoids those allocations with a used array, but it special-cases inputs of length zero and one. It also copies the whole append, recurse and undo block for the two orientations, and repeats a similar block again for the first domino. A is clearer and has less repeated code.
